sections.preamble: You answer questions about a single medical image. Follow the answer format requested in the user message exactly.

content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a fibrous soft-tissue tumor.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

The tumor is the large bright mass on the image-left (patient right) side, spanning roughly x 85–215 and y 365–590 in the left panel.

In the right panel, which marks fall in that region?
- Mark 430 sits at about (788, 464), which corresponds to x≈100 in the left panel. That is near the left edge of the mass and may be inside it, but it is close to the border.
- Mark 367 sits at about (841, 496), which corresponds to x≈153 in the left panel. That is well within the mass, at about y=496.
- Mark 327 at (841, 443) is also inside the mass, but it is a triangle rather than one of the circle marks.
- Mark 318 at (833, 565) is near the lower part of the mass.

The mass center is approximately x≈150, y≈475 in the left panel. Mark 367 at (153, 496) is closest to that center.

ANSWER: 367
